chapter_name: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom and Poems
learning_objective: 🎯 Learn about the historical struggle against Apartheid in South Africa, the true meaning of courage, and the contrast between freedom and captivity in 'A Tiger in the Zoo'.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: This is an extract from Nelson Mandela’s autobiography. It describes the historic inauguration ceremony on May 10, 1994, when Mandela became South Africa’s first black President. He talks about the brutal 'Apartheid' (racial segregation) system and pays tribute to the thousands of patriots who sacrificed their lives for freedom.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🦅 Mandela's Views on Courage and Freedom
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Mandela redefines courage: it is not the absence of fear, but the triumph over it. He explains the 'Twin Obligations' every man has: one to his family, and one to his country. He also states a profound truth: the oppressor (the one who locks others up) is also not free, because he is a prisoner of hatred and prejudice.

main_concepts.concept_title: 🐅 A Tiger in the Zoo (Poem by Leslie Norris)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The poem creates a sharp contrast between a tiger in a zoo and a tiger in its natural habitat (the jungle). In the zoo, the majestic animal is locked in a concrete cell, helpless, angry, and ignoring visitors. In the jungle, he would be sliding through long grass, hunting deer, and terrorizing the village. It highlights the cruelty of keeping wild animals in captivity.

fun_activity.title: 🐅 The Staring Tiger
fun_activity.instructions: In the poem, the caged tiger 'stares with his brilliant eyes at the brilliant stars.' Why? Because the stars represent freedom, vastness, and the natural world he belongs to. He cannot look at the humans (who put him there), so he looks up at the sky, dreaming of his lost freedom.

exam_tips: 📌 What are the 'Twin Obligations'? (1. To family/parents/wife/children. 2. To people/community/country). This is a guaranteed 2 or 3-mark question.
📌 Mandela says, 'The brave man is not he who does not feel afraid, but he who conquers that fear.' Memorize this quote for character-based questions.
📌 In the poem, contrast the tiger's actions: Zoo (paces quietly, ignores visitors, helpless) vs. Jungle (lurks in shadow, hunts plump deer, snarls at houses).
quick_recap: ⭐ The inauguration ceremony took place in the Union Buildings amphitheatre in Pretoria.
⭐ Mandela realized that freedom is indivisible; the chains on any one of his people were chains on all of them.
⭐ The Tiger’s 'velvet quiet' anger represents his suppressed power and helpless frustration inside the cage.
